sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the lilies work (2026-10-18): every character from the floras in the lilies notes (plantgen-claude project-files/lilies/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Lilium occidentale, plant_name_id 279991.

growth_form.note: A bulbous herb with one leafy flowering stem a year, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown five years from seed, as a lily bulb takes three to five to flower; drawn at its third and fifth years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

allometry.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: stems usually 0.6-1.5 m; FNA gives only 'stems to 2.2 m'. Its reference height is the middle of that range, 1.05 m, at its last keyframe.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: stems usually 0.6-1.5 m; FNA gives only 'stems to 2.2 m'.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): stems to 2.2 m

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): leaves scattered or in 1-9 whorls or partial whorls

traits.leaf_whorls.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): in 1-9 whorls. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): 3-19 leaves per whorl. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): leaves 4.1-26.3 x 0.4-3 cm. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): leaves 0.4-3 cm wide, 4-29 times longer than wide. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): blade elliptic to linear, occasionally narrowly lanceolate

traits.leaf_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): horizontal and drooping at tips to ascending

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): inflorescences racemose, 1-35-flowered. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.flower_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): flowers pendent, not fragrant

traits.perianth_reflexion.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): perianth Turk's-cap-shaped; sepals and petals reflexed 2/5 along length from base

traits.perianth_reflexion_from.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): reflexed 2/5 along length from base

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): yellow, greenish yellow or green proximally, then red-orange to red to maroon on the distal 1/2-2/3; drawn in the distal red, the showier share The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.perianth_base_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): yellow, greenish yellow, or green proximally The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.perianth_base_length.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): red-orange to red to maroon or very rarely orange on distal 1/2-2/3, so the proximal 1/3-1/2 in its base colour

traits.nectary_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): green proximally (and usually forming a green star) The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.perianth_spots.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): maroon, dark purple or rarely blackish spots concentrated proximally

traits.perianth_spot_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): maroon or dark purple spots The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.tepal_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): sepals 4.4-8.1 cm, petals 4.3-8 cm

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): stamens moderately exserted

traits.anther_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): anthers dull red, dull purple or magenta The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.pedicel_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): pedicel 5-29.7 cm. The typical value is our pick of a usual plant inside that range.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): capsules 2.1-5.4 x 1-1.9 cm

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): capsules 1-1.9 cm wide

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 26 (2002), Lilium occidentale (efloras.org, read 2026-10-18): flowering summer (Jun-Aug)
